decisions.evidence: The five long oblique strokes cancel this paragraph. In the space between G and il there is no distinct dark comma; remove the supplied comma. The broken raffine-/ment is one word continued on the following manuscript line. The blind inclusion of the next Ainsi fragment is a box-boundary difference; it is already separately transcribed and cancelled.

The strike crosses the middle of the word after Ainsi. A d ascender and low final run favour dans, but the other letters do not become individually clear. Retain the existing alternatives rather than resolve a cancelled doubt from context.

The initial évid is readable; its compressed continuation has raised terminal strokes. Retain the short-form transcription with an uncertain ending. The blind full expansion is not established by individually legible letters.

The whole proof-heading line and the tight crop show a tall I, low compressed middle groups and a final t whose base lies on the same baseline. Prefer the blind baseline short form Inversemt; keep the formerly read raised ending and full-word alternative explicitly doubtful.

The strike covers the middle and final letters of Sinon. Initial S and the i dot survive, but not every cancelled letter is independently plain. Add a doubt mark to Sinon. The descending comma sits below and beyond the strike and remains live.

The complete two-line formula was reread. After the singleton there are three low letter groups, with an angular middle v-like return and an open final c-like ending, favouring avec over the earlier où; retain the latter as an alternative. The edge has x∈|F| followed by a lowered K-like/brace-like mark, not a separately established slash and additional G. Adopt the doubtful lowered mark. Keep the uncertain P alphabet, cancelled g, and the clear second-line index |F| minus |G|, despite its mathematical difficulty.

The overwritten letter has a small bowl and a long hooked descender under the crossing stroke. These support the existing doubtful g. The blind f alternative does not establish a different preferred letter; retain the first reading with its doubt.

After the tall bars enclosing a clear F, the ink drops down at the paper edge. The lowered cluster has a stem and two diverging arms, K-like, and might instead belong to a closing brace. There is no separately readable set-difference slash followed by G. Replace that conjectural extension by the blind lowered-K/brace alternative, without supplying a certain closing delimiter.

The heading underline ends beneath Dém, before the following full stop; retain that punctuation scope. The two short forms have been checked in their own crops: keep doubtful raised évid-ending, change Inversemt to a doubtful baseline short form. Supposons starts the next line beyond this box and remains in the complete page.
